Now we’re talking.

blocks.text: The fullness that contains everything while transcending everything.
blocks.directed: The fullness that contains everything while transcending everything.

blocks.text: Remember how we began the whole Tantrasāra?
blocks.directed: Remember how we began the whole Tantrasāra?

blocks.text: Śiva is both immanent and transcendent.
blocks.directed: Śiva is both immanent and transcendent.

blocks.text: Of the nature of the universe.
blocks.directed: Of the nature of the universe.

blocks.text: Well, here’s the same fundamental principle expressed through the analysis of states.

blocks.text: The supreme reality is not merely one state competing with other states.
blocks.directed: The supreme reality is not merely one state competing with other states.

blocks.text: It is the fullness in which all states arise.
blocks.directed: It is the fullness in which all states arise.

blocks.text: The great fullness or supreme accumulation.
blocks.directed: The great fullness or supreme accumulation.

blocks.text: Because if you imagine liberation as entering Turya and staying there forever, you’ve still potentially constructed an opposition between the fourth state and ordinary waking experience.

blocks.text: But Turyātīta is not defined through that exclusion.

blocks.text: It’s the all-inclusive fullness that transcends every limitation.
blocks.directed: It’s the all-inclusive fullness that transcends every limitation.

blocks.text: Not merely consciousness without the world, but consciousness whose freedom includes the entire world.
blocks.directed: Not merely consciousness without the world, but consciousness whose freedom includes the entire world.

blocks.text: And this brings us back to the seven subjects.

blocks.text: Because Abhinavagupta is about to connect the five states of consciousness with the various levels of knowership.

blocks.text: Abhinavagupta says the term waking can be used wherever an appearance is clear, stable and continuously connected.

blocks.text: The condition of non-difference between every existent thing and Śiva.
blocks.directed: The condition of non-difference between every existent thing and Śiva.

blocks.text: The same categories we’ve been analysing as kinds of subjectivity can also be understood through the configurations of conscious experience.
blocks.directed: The same categories we’ve been analysing as kinds of subjectivity can also be understood through the configurations of conscious experience.

blocks.text: And Abhinavagupta then gives a series of correspondences between the different numerical divisions and the five states.
blocks.directed: And Abhinavagupta then gives a series of correspondences between the different numerical divisions and the five states.

blocks.text: In the fifteenfold system, the own-nature of the object together with Sakala is associated with waking.
blocks.directed: In the fifteenfold system, the own-nature of the object together with Sakala is associated with waking.

blocks.directed: The group comprising Mantra, Mantreśvara and Mantramaheśvara with Turya.

blocks.text: But as we move upward through the thirteenfold, elevenfold, ninefold, sevenfold, fivefold and threefold arrangements, the specific allocations change.
blocks.directed: But as we move upward through the thirteenfold, elevenfold, ninefold, sevenfold, fivefold and threefold arrangements, the specific allocations change.

blocks.text: Because the lower forms of knowing subjectivity have ceased to apply.
blocks.directed: Because the lower forms of knowing subjectivity have ceased to apply.

blocks.text: And even within the undivided Śiva-tattva, contemplative analysis can provisionally distinguish five aspects through:

blocks.directed: Now, at the end of Chapter Nine, we’ve arrived back at those same five powers.

blocks.text: But we’ve understood that even their distinction is an analytical construction within the fullness of Śiva.
blocks.directed: But we’ve understood that even their distinction is an analytical construction within the fullness of Śiva.

blocks.text: The same consciousness manifests the many, experiences the many, and recognises the many as itself.

blocks.text: Among all the tattvas beginning with earth, there is no form whatsoever that fails to rest in the consciousness of the knower.
blocks.directed: Among all the tattvas beginning with earth, there is no form whatsoever that fails to rest in the consciousness of the knower.

blocks.text: Because the nature of the knower shines forth in manifold ways.
blocks.directed: Because the nature of the knower shines forth in manifold ways.

blocks.text: Now think about the entire chapter.
blocks.directed: Now think about the entire chapter.

blocks.text: We began with seven different knowing subjects.
blocks.directed: We began with seven different knowing subjects.

blocks.text: Then the seven powers through which those subjects apprehend their objects.
blocks.directed: Then the seven powers through which those subjects apprehend their objects.

blocks.text: Then the fifteenfold structure of manifestation.
blocks.directed: Then the fifteenfold structure of manifestation.

blocks.text: Then the progressively smaller sets of distinctions.
blocks.directed: Then the progressively smaller sets of distinctions.

blocks.text: Then the emergence of cognition through the minute movements of prāṇa.
blocks.directed: Then the emergence of cognition through the minute movements of prāṇa.

blocks.text: Then waking, dreaming, deep sleep, Turya and Turyātīta.
blocks.directed: Then waking, dreaming, deep sleep, Turya and Turyātīta.
[short pause] And now Abhinavagupta tells you:

blocks.text: Nothing in the entire network of reality is without repose in consciousness.
blocks.directed: Nothing in the entire network of reality is without repose in consciousness.

blocks.text: Within this entire network of knowable things, establish yourselves in the state where conceptual succession is transcended.
blocks.directed: Within this entire network of knowable things, establish yourselves in the state where conceptual succession is transcended.

blocks.text: The state whose essence is the apprehension of the absolute freedom of I-consciousness.
blocks.directed: The state whose essence is the apprehension of the absolute freedom of I-consciousness.

blocks.text: Not the constructed ego from Chapter Eight.
blocks.directed: Not the constructed ego from Chapter Eight.

blocks.text: Not the little identity that says:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Not the little identity that says:

blocks.text: The unrestricted I-consciousness through which all these limited manifestations appear.
blocks.directed: The unrestricted I-consciousness through which all these limited manifestations appear.

blocks.text: Attain the true being of your own Self.
blocks.directed: Attain the true being of your own Self.

blocks.text: Now that’s a rather extraordinary ending.
blocks.directed: Now that’s a rather extraordinary ending.
[short pause] Because we began by asking:

blocks.text: “How can seven different subjects experience the same universe differently?”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “How can seven different subjects experience the same universe differently?”

blocks.text: The same supreme consciousness manifests multiple modes of knowership, multiple modes of cognition and multiple modes of objectivity.
blocks.directed: The same supreme consciousness manifests multiple modes of knowership, multiple modes of cognition and multiple modes of objectivity.

blocks.text: But none of these divisions establishes an independent reality outside consciousness.
blocks.directed: But none of these divisions establishes an independent reality outside consciousness.

blocks.text: And as the distinctions subside, the underlying freedom becomes increasingly evident.
blocks.directed: And as the distinctions subside, the underlying freedom becomes increasingly evident.

blocks.text: Until, at the highest level, no division remains.
blocks.directed: Until, at the highest level, no division remains.

blocks.text: Now, here’s what I find particularly beautiful.
blocks.directed: Now, here’s what I find particularly beautiful.

blocks.text: You don’t have to imagine that the entire universe disappears in liberation.
blocks.directed: You don’t have to imagine that the entire universe disappears in liberation.

blocks.text: The mind can continue forming concepts.
blocks.directed: The mind can continue forming concepts.

blocks.text: But the fundamental understanding is no longer restricted to the opposition between a little subject and a separate world.
blocks.directed: But the fundamental understanding is no longer restricted to the opposition between a little subject and a separate world.

blocks.text: The universe is apprehended as the manifold expression of the one conscious Self.
blocks.directed: The universe is apprehended as the manifold expression of the one conscious Self.

blocks.text: And the seven kinds of knower?
blocks.directed: And the seven kinds of knower?

blocks.text: Different expressions of that Self’s own powers.
blocks.directed: Different expressions of that Self’s own powers.

blocks.text: Something you’ve done a thousand times.
blocks.directed: Something you’ve done a thousand times.

blocks.text: But according to Abhinavagupta, that apparently simple act involves the entire metaphysical structure of experience.
blocks.directed: But according to Abhinavagupta, that apparently simple act involves the entire metaphysical structure of experience.

blocks.text: And the conscious freedom through which all of these arise.
blocks.directed: And the conscious freedom through which all of these arise.

blocks.text: You’ve spent your whole life thinking you’re a little bloke looking at things.
blocks.directed: You’ve spent your whole life thinking you’re a little bloke looking at things.

blocks.text: And Abhinavagupta has just spent an entire chapter explaining that the very possibility of looking at anything is an expression of Śiva’s own self-awareness.
